title: Riga over 4,000 years
episode: Evolution of Riga (2000 BC–2026): 4,000 Years from One Fixed View
description: An animation of one view of Riga changing over 4,000 years, from fishing villages on the Daugava to the medieval town, the Russian imperial port, and the modern city. St. Peter’s tower has the best real view.

title: The Art Nouveau capital
episode: How Riga Became Europe's Art Nouveau Capital
place: Riga Art Nouveau Centre, Alberta iela 12
description: A talk on how a building boom around 1900 left Riga with about a third of its center in Art Nouveau, including the wild facades of Mikhail Eisenstein, father of the film director Sergei Eisenstein, on Alberta iela.

title: The Corner House
episode: The Corner House: Latvia's KGB Headquarters
description: A tour of the Corner House, the KGB’s Riga headquarters, where suspects were interrogated and held in cells in the basement. People called it the tallest building in Riga, because from its basement you could see Siberia.

title: The Baltic Way
episode: Baltic Way 1989 Achieving the Unthinkable  - Documentary by Kristine S.
description: On August 23, 1989, about two million people joined hands in a chain from Tallinn through Riga to Vilnius, protesting the 1939 Nazi-Soviet pact that led to the occupation. The chain passed the Freedom Monument.

title: Forbidden songs
description: How Latvian choirs sang patriotic songs the Soviet authorities had banned, and how the song festivals became acts of defiance. The festival, held every five years, fills this open-air stage with thousands of singers.

title: January 1991
description: Footage of the barricades in January 1991. On the night of January 20, Soviet special police attacked the Interior Ministry, and five people were killed in and around this park, including two cameramen. Stones mark where they fell.

title: The Baltic languages
episode: The BALTIC Languages (Lithuanian, Latvian, and Beyond)
description: A linguist on Latvian and Lithuanian, the last surviving Baltic languages, which keep many very old Indo-European features. The national library across the river echoes the Castle of Light from Latvian poetry and folklore.

title: Riga’s Russian speakers
description: A documentary on Latvia’s large Russian-speaking minority, many of whom came in Soviet times, and the tensions over language and citizenship since independence. The Stalin-era Academy of Sciences tower looms over the Moscow district.
